Dear [Mr Craik](/person/379)
The printer can judge better than I but I do not think there is enough of [the Quest of Ulysses](/book/185) to make more than such a volume as [the Little Duke](/book/20), so I think it had better belong to that Series.
Thank you for Lord Albemarles’ memoirs. I was waiting to do so till I saw what [Mudie](/organisation/137) sent me, and his box is either delayed or lost, as I have just discovered.
I will not close this letter till I hear the result of the enquiry I have sent to make at the Parcels’ Office. If I do not get the books today, I think I must ask you to let me have the Queens Journals the Greville Memoirs Princess Alice, and Lady Blomfield, in all of which I know there are characteristic bits.[^1] I have just down the year of revolutions, but I cannot finish off the beginning without more authorities.
The Annals are very useful. Unluckily this copy has Sheet M twice over, and no sheet N but I do not think there is anything very important in the missing one[^2]

Yours truly

C M Yonge		
Perhaps I ought to see Madame Bunsen’s memoirs
No books come - so if you would kindly get them for me


[^1]: These books were all wanted for CMY\'s work on [Victorian Half-Century](/book/189).
[^2]: Craik had presumably provided her with the most recent (1880) edition of Joseph Irving, The Annals of our Time.
